title: idfkit conformance manifest
description: Index over every conformance case: its id, its tags, and which of the four assertions apply. Cases carrying an externally produced expectation live in the 'oracle' section; cases resting on agreed convention live in the 'convention' section, so agreed convention is never mistaken for external truth (FR-020). Claims about a library's behaviour rather than about a document's content are not cases at all: they are indexed in 'checks', and each carries its own directory, fixtures, committed expectations and check.md.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editor completion and offline validation.

schema_version.description: Version of the manifest format itself. Bumped only by a change that breaks readers.

corpus_level.description: The immutable level tag this manifest state was published as, of the form conformance-YYYY.N. Null while the level is unpublished.

oracle.description: Cases whose expectation was produced by the external authority, EnergyPlus ConvertInputFormat. Every entry carries an 'expected' file.

convention.description: Cases resting on agreed convention between the two libraries. No external authority produced an expectation, so no entry may carry an 'expected' file.

checks.description: Claims about a library's behaviour, each a directory under checks/ carrying its own check.md, fixtures and committed expectations. Absent while the corpus has none. A check is not a case: it has no input document, no epJSON expectation, and no place in either section above.

check.description: One check: the directory it lives in, what it asserts, and which libraries have a recorded result.

id.description: Slug identifying the check. Also the directory name under checks/.

title.description: One line saying what is claimed.

path.description: The check's directory, relative to the repository root.

assertions.description: The check's own assertion names, stated in its check.md and mirrored by its runners. Deliberately not the case assertion taxonomy: a check states what it asserts rather than drawing from a fixed enum, because the shape of the claim differs from check to check.

libraries.description: The libraries whose result this check records at this level. A library absent here has not run the check, which is a gap rather than a failure.

caseId.description: Slug identifying the case. Also the directory name under cases/, and the key the exception register refers to.

tag.description: Hazard the case pins, from the corpus taxonomy. 'tier1' marks the one case per Tier 1 capability ported in this feature.

assertion.description: One assertion. 'diagnostics' is accepted and skipped by the runners until phase two. 'validation', 'introspection' and 'docs-url' are the Tier 1 assertions, which have no oracle behind them; see runners/compare.md. 'type-lookup' has no oracle either and asks a different question from every other assertion: not what a library made of a file, but what it returns when a caller names an object type. 'preserved-text' is the one byte-level assertion and is not 'round-trip' under another name: round-trip re-reads a library's own output and compares documents, saying nothing about the bytes in between, and it writes with preservation explicitly OFF for that reason. preserved-text asserts the echo that would make round-trip trivially true, deliberately.

case.description: One case entry. Shared by both sections; the section decides whether 'expected' is required or forbidden.

title.description: One line, matching the 'title' in the case's own case.toml.

tags.description: The hazards this case pins. At least one.

energyplus_version.description: The EnergyPlus release whose ConvertInputFormat produced the expectation, or whose schema the case is written against (FR-014).

assertions.description: Which of the four assertions the runners apply to this case. At least one.

input.description: The case input, relative to the case directory. The extension tells the runner which reader to dispatch to.

parse_outcome.description: What reading the input is declared to do. The 'parse-outcome' assertion checks this.

expected.description: The committed epJSON expectation, relative to the case directory. Required in the 'oracle' section, forbidden in the 'convention' section.

expected_diagnostics.description: Expected diagnostics file, relative to the case directory. Required when 'assertions' includes 'diagnostics', forbidden otherwise.

expected_validation.description: Expected validation findings, relative to the case directory. Required when 'assertions' includes 'validation', forbidden otherwise.

expected_introspection.description: Expected type descriptions, relative to the case directory. Required when 'assertions' includes 'introspection', forbidden otherwise.

expected_docs_url.description: Expected documentation addresses, relative to the case directory. Required when 'assertions' includes 'docs-url', forbidden otherwise.

expected_type_lookup.description: Expected collection lookups by object type name, relative to the case directory. Required when 'assertions' includes 'type-lookup', forbidden otherwise.

operations.description: Changes to apply to the document between reading and writing, in list order. Language-neutral: each runner maps the four kinds onto its own library's mutators, exactly as 'writer_options' already does for the five writer controls. ABSENT MEANS READ ONLY, which is what all 56 pre-existing cases mean and must keep meaning. A case declaring operations alongside 'preserved-text' narrows that assertion to the property FR-023 states: every byte outside the extents of the objects these operations touched equals the input. The four kinds are the four the touched record has to get right, and no more; a fifth is added when a claim needs it, not in advance.

writer_options.description: Writer controls to apply before re-reading, in the 'round-trip' assertion. Language-neutral names: each runner maps them onto its own writer's option. Absent means every writer default, which is what all 48 pre-existing cases mean and must keep meaning. A case that sets one is asserting FR-019: a document written under that control re-reads to the same structure.

comments.description: Emit field-name comments. Python 'output_type=nocomment' when false; TypeScript 'comments'.

compressed.description: One object per line, no comments, no blank separators. Python 'output_type=compressed'; TypeScript 'compressed'.

indent.description: Spaces before each field line. Python 'indent' (a count); TypeScript 'indent' (a string, which the runner builds from this count).

comment_column.description: Column the field-name comments are padded to. Python 'comment_column'; TypeScript 'commentColumn'.

ordering.description: How objects are ordered. 'sorted' is by type name; 'source' is the document's own order. An enumeration rather than a boolean because three behaviours exist across the two languages and two formats.

operation.description: One change to the document, applied before the write. 'type' and 'name' identify the object in language-neutral terms; a name is required even for a type that carries none, in which case it is the collection key the runner looks the object up by.

op.description: Which change. 'set-field' writes one field; 'rename' changes an object's name and retargets every reference to it; 'remove' takes an object out of the document; 'add' puts a new one in.

type.description: The object's type name, as the schema spells it.

name.description: The object's name. For 'add', the name the new object takes.

field.description: The epJSON field name to write. Required by 'set-field', forbidden otherwise.

value.description: The value to write, as text. Each runner coerces it the way its own reader coerces a value read from a file, so a case says what a file would have said. Required by 'set-field', forbidden otherwise.

to.description: The new name. Required by 'rename', forbidden otherwise.

fields.description: Field values for the new object, as text. Optional on 'add', forbidden otherwise.

expectationRule.description: One rule per assertion that reads an expectation file: declaring the assertion requires the file, and not declaring it forbids naming one. Kept as parallel entries rather than one parameterised rule because JSON Schema has no way to express the parameter.

oracleCase.description: A case with truth = oracle. Its expectation was generated offline by ConvertInputFormat and committed.

conventionCase.description: A case with truth = convention. No external authority produced an expectation.
